subject: Redlines: Governing Law, Interim Relief & Jurisdictional Sequence (Skybridge Health)
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@skybridgehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Catherine Lee <clee@bromleylaw.com>, Evan Jacobs <evan.jacobs@skybridgehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-05 09:12 PDT
Subject: Skybridge MSA redlines - governing law & injunctive relief

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the draft MSA. Our legal team has redlined Governing Law, Dispute Resolution and the Equitable Relief carve (attached: MSA_Skybridge_redline.docx). High-level asks: we prefer Delaware law but need a carve to allow Skybridge to seek emergency injunctive relief in California courts (our HQ) while preserving arbitration for monetary claims.

Specific items we flagged:
- A clear sequence for emergency relief vs. arbitration (we want the ability to go to CA court immediately to preserve evidence or obtain an ex parte freeze).
- A statement that emergency equitable relief does not waive Skybridge's right to arbitration for damages.
- Clarify service-of-process and consent-to-venue for provisional measures.
- Bond/undertaking language for injunctive relief (we expect Redwood to waive or cap any bond in the case of clear confidentiality breaches).

Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept: (1) Delaware law as the governing law; and (2) an injunctive carve that allows Skybridge to file for provisional relief in CA state or federal court (customer's election) with the merits to be decided in arbitration? If not, what alternatives would you consider?

We're on a short timetable — aiming to finalize the order form and sign by next week.

Best,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Procurement, Skybridge Health
sofia.ramos@skybridgehealth.com
Attachment: MSA_Skybridge_redline.docx (redline)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@skybridgehealth.com>, Catherine Lee <clee@bromleylaw.com>
Date: 2026-10-05 10:30 PDT
Subject: Re: Skybridge MSA redlines - governing law & injunctive relief

Team — looping you in. Sofia's redline asks for Delaware governing law + a broad customer right to seek injunctive relief in CA. Sketching our concerns and an initial counter for counsel:

1) Broad litigation carveouts are risky — if we allow free-for-all forum shopping we lose predictability for emergency handling and may create conflicting orders.
2) We can accept provisional relief being sought in customer's local courts for true emergency preservation (e.g., ex parte preservation of KV cache or immediate stop of data exfiltration), but we should: 
   - Narrow the carve to narrowly-defined "emergency equitable relief to preserve the status quo or prevent imminent, irreparable harm";
   - Require that any emergency relief applicant file for arbitration on the merits within 30 days of seeking provisional measures;
   - Limit venue to state or federal courts located in the customer's principal place of business.
3) We should push back on blanket waivers of bond; acceptable compromise is to commit to good-faith application for bond waiver only where the order requires disclosure of Redwood trade secrets or where we are unable to post security promptly.

I've drafted a short counter-redline. Attaching: Redwood_counter_redline_v1.docx. Marcus / Jonas — any procedural or litigation risk notes?

Olga Petrov
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_counter_redline_v1.docx

From: Catherine Lee <clee@bromleylaw.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@skybridgehealth.com>, Evan Jacobs <evan.jacobs@skybridgehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-06 14:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Skybridge MSA redlines - governing law & injunctive relief

Olga/Counsel — thanks for the quick note. A few responses from Skybridge and our outside counsel: 

- Skybridge prefers Delaware law for predictability, but they will not agree to a 30-day arbitration-filing deadline after obtaining provisional relief; that could effectively deny them protection in time-sensitive situations.
- They want clear language that seeking provisional relief in a court does not constitute a waiver of arbitration rights for the merits, and (separately) they need confirmation Redwood will not assert a jurisdictional defense to bar provisional measures in their chosen court.
- On bonds: Skybridge is open to a reasonable undertaking but will not accept an automatic posted bond equal to the requested relief amount. They propose language: "courts may require security in accordance with applicable law; parties agree to request a reduced undertaking where disclosure of Redwood's confidential information would be required."
- Quick practical ask: can Redwood confirm which jurisdictions it considers "customer's principal place of business" for forum limitation purposes? Skybridge's entity is incorporated in Delaware but has HQ in San Francisco; they want the option of CA or DE.

Proposed compromise (high-level): 
1) Governing law: Delaware.
2) Emergency interim measures: customer may seek provisional equitable relief in a court located in the customer's principal place of business (CA) or where the material harm occurs. Such relief does not waive arbitration of the dispute's merits; the parties agree to promptly proceed to arbitration on the merits, but no fixed 30-day filing deadline.
3) Undertaking: courts may require a bond; parties agree to seek a reduced bond where confidentiality risk is present.

If Redwood can accept the above in principle, Skybridge would like a short call to finalize the interplay language and then execute the order form.

Catherine Lee
Bromley & Associates, Outside Counsel to Skybridge Health
clee@bromleylaw.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@skybridgehealth.com>, Catherine Lee <clee@bromleylaw.com>
Date: 2026-10-06 16:20 PDT
Subject: Re: Skybridge MSA redlines - governing law & injunctive relief

Thanks — quick internal note on risk posture and a narrower drafting approach we could propose on the call: 

- We should avoid open-ended dual-jurisdiction outcomes. Practical compromise: accept Delaware governing law for interpretation of contract terms, but permit provisional injunctive relief in courts located in the customer's principal place of business (e.g., CA) solely for preservation measures. For any other emergency relief beyond preservation (e.g., a temporary injunction changing service behavior), require a best-efforts meet-and-confer and immediate referral to arbitration.
- Replace a fixed arbitration filing deadline with a "reasonable promptness" standard and an obligation to escalate to arbitration administrator within 21 days of provisional relief being sought (this gives both sides certainty without being draconian).
- On bond: Redwood will agree to request a reduced undertaking where the court's order would require disclosure of Redwood confidential material; we should avoid absolute waivers.

Draft language I recommend we test on the call: "Nothing in this Agreement prevents either party from seeking urgent provisional equitable relief in a court in the applicant's principal place of business to preserve the status quo or prevent irreparable harm; such provisional relief shall be limited to preservation measures and shall not constitute a waiver of the right to arbitration on the merits. The party seeking provisional relief shall commence arbitration proceedings with reasonable promptness thereafter and shall use best efforts to have any provisional relief modified or vacated as appropriate upon appointment of an arbitrator."

If OK, Olga let's tee up a 30-minute call tomorrow with Skybridge counsel to agree language so we can push the order form.

Marcus Lin
Director, Litigation & External Counsel Partnerships
marcus.lin@redwood.com
